title: Shared Genetic Risk Between Acute Pancreatitis and Metabolic Syndrome Converges on a BCAT1-Positive Fibroblast Subpopulation and MAPK14-Driven Inflammation.
authors: Zhou, Xiaoying; Yang, Chen; Zou, Tongxin; Basharat, Zarrin; Zippi, Maddalena; Fiorino, Sirio; Hong, Wandong
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
one_liner_zh: 该文通过遗传与转录组分析急性胰腺炎与代谢综合征共享基因，含转录因子映射和分子对接，但核心是炎症与成纤维细胞机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，方法上仅浅层涉及TF映射与对接，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) has been associated with increased acute pancreatitis (AP) severity. This study aimed to identify shared differentially expressed genes (CDEGs) between MetS and AP and to prioritize mechanistically relevant targets. The shared genetic basis and causal effect of MetS on AP were first assessed using linkage disequilibrium score regression (LDSC) and two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Public Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets were analyzed to define shared CDEGs. A multi-step pipeline incorporating functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, and transcription factor mapping was used to identify AP hub genes (AP-HGs). Functional relatedness and putative causal relationships were evaluated using GeneMANIA, MR, and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). Finally, computational drug prediction and molecular docking were performed to identify potential therapeutic agents. Key findings were further validated in a hyperlipidemia AP (HAP) model. A positive genetic correlation between MetS and AP was identified by LDSC, and MR supported a causal effect of MetS on increased AP risk. BCAT1, GPAT3, ANP32C, and ZNF683 were identified as CDEGs between MetS and AP. MAPK14 was identified as a central AP-HG. MAPK14, BCAT1, and GPAT3 were effective predictors for severe AP (SAP), with AUCs of 0.738, 0.722, and 0.744, respectively. GeneMANIA predicted a high degree of physical interaction (77.6%) among these genes. MR analysis provided supportive genetic evidence linking MAPK14 expression to inflammatory mediators including IL-1ra and TNFR-1. scRNA-seq analysis in an experimental AP model localized Mapk14 expression predominantly to macrophages, while Bcat1 marked a unique, proliferative fibroblast subpopulation that emerged transiently during inflammation and exhibited an anabolic metabolic signature. Ozagrel was prioritized as an exploratory candidate with favorable predicted binding affinities and requires further validation. In a HAP model, aggravated pancreatic injury and upregulation of BCAT1 and MAPK14 were confirmed under the high-fat background. A genetic and transcriptomic link between MetS and AP was identified. MAPK14-associated inflammation and Bcat1-positive fibroblast remodeling may contribute to AP aggravation under metabolic disturbance. These findings provide candidate biomarkers for SAP prediction and support BCAT1 and MAPK14 as potential mechanistic targets.
abstract_zh: 代谢综合征（MetS）与急性胰腺炎（AP）严重程度增加相关。本研究旨在识别MetS与AP之间的共享差异表达基因（CDEGs），并优先筛选具有机制相关性的靶点。首先，利用连锁不平衡评分回归（LDSC）和双样本孟德尔随机化（MR）评估了MetS与AP的共享遗传基础及MetS对AP的因果效应。分析了公共基因表达综合数据库（GEO）数据集以确定共享CDEGs。采用包含功能富集、蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）分析和转录因子映射的多步骤流程，识别AP枢纽基因（AP-HGs）。利用GeneMANIA、MR和单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）评估功能相关性和推定因果关系。最后，进行计算药物预测和分子对接以识别潜在治疗药物。关键发现在高脂血症AP（HAP）模型中进一步验证。LDSC识别出MetS与AP之间存在正遗传相关性，MR支持MetS对AP风险增加的因果效应。BCAT1、GPAT3、ANP32C和ZNF683被识别为MetS与AP之间的CDEGs。MAPK14被识别为核心AP-HG。MAPK14、BCAT1和GPAT3是重症AP（SAP）的有效预测因子，AUC分别为0.738、0.722和0.744。GeneMANIA预测这些基因之间存在高度物理相互作用（77.6%）。MR分析提供了支持性遗传证据，将MAPK14表达与炎症介质（包括IL-1ra和TNFR-1）相关联。实验性AP模型中的scRNA-seq分析显示，Mapk14表达主要定位于巨噬细胞，而Bcat1标记了一个独特的、增殖性成纤维细胞亚群，该亚群在炎症期间短暂出现并表现出合成代谢代谢特征。奥扎格雷（Ozagrel）被优先列为探索性候选药物，具有有利的预测结合亲和力，需进一步验证。在HAP模型中，高脂背景下胰腺损伤加重以及BCAT1和MAPK14的上调得到确认。识别出MetS与AP之间的遗传和转录组联系。MAPK14相关炎症和Bcat1阳性成纤维细胞重塑可能促进代谢紊乱下AP的加重。这些发现为SAP预测提供了候选生物标志物，并支持BCAT1和MAPK14作为潜在机制靶点。
